title: The Grain Shipment
subtitle: A corroboration warm-up
summary: Four accounts of one event disagree. Students work out which statement the evidence can carry — and meet a round where the honest answer is that it cannot be settled.
social_topology: Individual copies, or pairs on one device
sources_rights: No real sources are used. Every document is invented for the exercise.

human_tests.note: Opened as a file:// URL and played to the ending; the page loaded no resources beyond itself.
Every control focused and activated without a pointer, with a visible focus outline at each step.
Estimated at 3-5 minutes of reading from a 557-word path, not timed with a player.
No classroom setup to test against. The instructor must do this.
There are no real sources to check against. The game states this on its Sources & assumptions screen.
Five debrief questions ship on the ending screen.

provenance_note: This game uses no historical sources at all. Every document in it is invented to demonstrate the format and to carry a specific source-criticism problem. It is a method exercise, not a history lesson.
